content.comment_body: Is it possible to use the [product_name] Android app within a network that uses a dynamic IP address? Is there any solution to keep using the app even if my address changes every day or two?

You can use a dynamic DNS service with the app. As far as I know, the app currently only supports dyndns. Check the ‘Interface configure’ section and, instead of selecting an IP address, use a dyndns address and pick that option in the app settings.
Unfortunately, my background is in high voltage engineering and I’m not familiar with DNS. Could you provide some guidance? That would be very helpful. Thank you in advance. [user_name]

Hello [user_name], It’s best to visit: [url] You can create an account for about $25 per year and get a dyndns hostname. Instead of using an IP address, you would use a hostname like myhost.dyndns.org, or another name you choose. This static hostname replaces your frequently changing IP address, making it easier to remember. In the app, enter the hostname instead of the IP address when setting up a connection. How does dyndns keep track of your changing IP address? There are two ways: your router might support dyndns (check your router’s settings for this option). If so, you can enter the dyndns hostname there—each time your router connects to the internet, it automatically sends the new IP to dyndns and updates your hostname. If your router does not support dyndns, you can install a program on your PC that updates dyndns with your current IP address after every boot. Hope this helps!

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience difficulties connecting remotely to their [product_name] system using the Android app when the IP address changes frequently. The app currently requires using a dynamic DNS service (such as dyndns), which complicates things for users with limited DNS knowledge. Users are seeking a simple connectivity solution and guidance on handling dynamic IP changes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the Android app to provide seamless connectivity regardless of IP address changes, requiring minimal technical setup. They prefer clear instructions or automated solutions to manage dynamic IP scenarios easily.
